key_insight: Overconfidence in deep neural networks originates largely from standard initialization practices; a brief, brain-inspired warm-up training using random noise immediately after initialization substantially improves uncertainty calibration and the model's ability to recognize unknown inputs.
problem_solved: Addresses excessive model overconfidence and poor uncertainty estimates (including failure to recognize out-of-distribution / unknown inputs) that arise from conventional network initialization and training pipelines.
method: Insert a short warm-up training phase right after initialization using random-noise inputs (brain-inspired perturbation to early learning).
This warm-up alters early weight statistics/representations so subsequent standard training produces better-calibrated predictive probabilities.
Assess improvements via calibration metrics and meta-cognitive tests for unknown / out-of-distribution detection.
impact: A simple, low-cost intervention (no architecture changes) that improves reliability of uncertainty estimates and unknown detection—valuable for deploying safer, more trustworthy ML systems in practice.
visual_elements: Before/after reliability diagrams (calibration curves) showing reduced overconfidence and lower Expected Calibration Error (ECE).
Training timeline schematic highlighting the brief 'warm-up with random noise' stage followed by normal training.
Comparison bar/line charts of OOD/unknown detection metrics (AUROC, FPR@95) with vs. without warm-up.
Iconic brain-inspired graphic illustrating noisy input perturbation to initial weights to emphasize biological motivation.
paper_title: Brain-inspired warm-up training with random noise for uncertainty calibration
